Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 49, verse 1:

You can notice here the connection (munasabah) between this verse at the opening of Surat al-Hujurat and the end of Surat al-Fath. In the final verses of al-Fath, Almighty God told us about what took place at al-Hudaybiyah, how the situation there ended with the treaty (sulh), and how this treaty caused disagreement between the Messenger and those who believed in him.

We said: before they returned to Madinah, Almighty God informed them of the wisdom behind returning without performing the 'umrah this year. So, the believers had an opinion, and the Messenger of Allah had a different opinion, because the Muslims were zealous for themselves, whereas the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was zealous for Islam.

When opposition to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arose, Surat al-Hujurat came to address this matter in its first verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 1]. The address here is specifically to those who believe in Allah as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger.

﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 1] means: beware of putting forward an opinion or deciding a matter before Allah permits you to do so and His Messenger permits you and decides on it, because the Messenger of Allah does not speak except by revelation from Allah.

When you stand against the Messenger's command, you are in reality opposing the command of Allah, whom you have accepted as Lord and God and whose attributes you have believed in. The requirement of this faith is that you should not put your opinion before his opinion, nor your judgment before his judgment. So when Allah or the Messenger of Allah has spoken, do not put forward any opinion of your own.

The phrase ﴿before Allah and His Messenger...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 1] (bayna yadayh, "between his hands") means: in front of you, meaning do not get ahead of him by deciding a matter without him. Remember that you are before Allah and in His presence; He does not require you to move right or left.

His saying ﴿And fear Allah...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 1] means: if you wish not to put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger, then fear Allah in this matter. That is, do not be deceivers in it, and do not return once more to opposition, for this is not acceptable.

﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Hujurat: 1] means: fear the One whose attributes are these, for He hears everything that is said, and knows everything that stirs in your souls, and nothing of your affairs is hidden from Him. Since you have believed in Him, obedience to Him and obedience to His Messenger has become obligatory upon you.

Then Almighty God says:

﴿O you who believe, do not raise your voices...﴾.

The call here is also addressed to those who believe: that they should not raise their voices above the voice of the Prophet in his presence, and likewise should not raise their opinion above his opinion. Among the etiquette of speech in general is that you do not raise your voice, for raising the voice carries arrogance, or at least equality. So what of when the one speaking to you is the Messenger of Allah?

Therefore: it is incumbent upon you that your voice not rise above his, but that your voice be lower and softer, and that you address him with courtesy and humility, just as you believed in him as a prophet and a messenger who conveys, and placed his opinion above your own.

Likewise, when you speak to him, do not raise your voice above his voice. His voice, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ought to be the highest, because he is the most deserving of being listened to and of being given attention. We are in a period of our history in which the saying (no voice rises above the voice of the battle) became widespread among us, because battle at that time was the solution. The meaning is: no voice rises above his voice.

﴿And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 2]. Do not call out to him as some of you call out to others, so we do not say: "Come here, O Ahmad! Come here, O Muhammad!" Rather we say: "O Prophet! O Messenger!" "O Messenger of Allah!" because your Lord, who created you and created him and sent him to you as a messenger, addressed him in this way.

Whereas He, exalted is He, addressed all the messengers by their names: "O Adam, O Noah, O Abraham, O Moses, O Jesus." But Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, He did not address by his name; rather by his attribute: "O Prophet" "O Messenger." So if his Creator did not call him by his name...

Therefore: it is incumbent upon you to call him by this attribute, unless you are higher in station than the One who created you, and Allah forbid.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿lest your deeds be nullified...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 2], that is: for fear that your deeds may be nullified. That is: they become void and corrupted. Why? Because speaking loudly to the Messenger of Allah in this manner, or raising the voice in his presence, is considered opposition to the method he brought.

The Messenger of Allah did not bring a method from himself; rather he is a conveyer from Allah. Whoever opposes in this has opposed the method of Allah and deserves to have his deed nullified. Moreover, insulting the Messenger is an insult to the one who sent him.

As for His saying: ﴿while you do not perceive﴾ [al-Hujurat: 2], that is: your deed is nullified and voided while you are unaware. This matter is one of the subtle things to which attention must be paid. Although he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is kind and merciful to the believers, do not let these qualities deceive you and cause you to treat him as equal to others in address. Rather, preserve for him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his station, his awe, and his honor, and do not make him like you in speech. This is like a man who spoils a servant so that the servant becomes presumptuous, until his master calls him and he does not answer.

Likewise, an Arab man entered upon a people whom he did not know and who did not know him. He said: "Peace be upon you, O people whose manners are good." They said: "How did you know the goodness of our manners?" He said: "I knew the goodness of your manners from the badness of your servants' manners," meaning: they pamper their servants and do not punish them.

It has been narrated from our master Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 3].

The meaning of ﴿They lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 3]: they lower them and speak in a hushed tone in his presence, out of respect and honour for him (ﷺ).

﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 3]: i.e., He has purified them and made them sincere, so that they become a place for piety and obedience, and for carrying the method of the Messenger of Allah to all people. They are qualified to carry this message, after Allah has cleansed their hearts, purified them and refined them from impurity, and removed from them the diseases of showing off, hypocrisy and weak faith.

Events have smelted them in the crucible of hardships, so that only those strong in creed remained in the ranks of faith, those able to bear the trust of this call.

Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143]. So the Messenger testifies that he conveyed to us, and we testify that we conveyed to the people.

This verse was revealed concerning a group who had captives. They came to the Messenger of Allah seeking to discuss his matter so that he would release them, but they erred in several respects:

First: They came to the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) from behind and did not come through the doors.

This is because they did not know in which chamber the Messenger of Allah was staying. Was he with Aisha? Or with Hafsa? Or with Umm Salama? Yet they knew that the Messenger of Allah had various tasks: a task with the people, a task with his family, and a task before that with his Lord.

So it was incumbent upon them, if the Messenger of Allah did not appear to them in the mosque, to wait for his emergence and not to disturb him, for he was certainly engaged in one of these tasks, and perhaps he was occupied in seclusion with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, or with his family.

Second: They called out to the Messenger of Allah as some of them call to one another, and did not observe the sanctity and station of the Messenger of Allah. Therefore most of them were described as not using their reason, for reason requires the opposite of this conduct.

﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them.﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 5] Indeed, it would have been better for them, because after they called out to him and compelled him to come out, the Prophet (ﷺ) released half of the captives and said: "By Allah, if they had been patient until I came out to them, I would have released all the captives."

He made that a discipline for them because they had departed from decorum and good manners in their dealings with him (ﷺ).

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 5]: He did not seize them with punishment, and the Messenger of Allah punished them according to the measure of their deeds, so that his anger would not be for his own sake.

Then the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He:

﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information...﴾.

This verse was revealed concerning a group who had captives. They came to the Messenger of Allah seeking to discuss his matter so that he would release them, but they erred in several respects:

First: They came to the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) from behind and did not come through the doors.

Second: They called out to the Messenger of Allah as some of them call to one another, and did not observe the sanctity and station of the Messenger of Allah. Therefore most of them were described as not using their reason, for reason requires the opposite of this conduct.

﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them.﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 5] Indeed, it would have been better for them, because after they called out to him and compelled him to come out, the Prophet (ﷺ) released half of the captives and said: "By Allah, if they had been patient until I came out to them, I would have released all the captives."

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 5]: He did not seize them with punishment, and the Messenger of Allah punished them according to the measure of their deeds, so that his anger would not be for his own sake.

Then the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He:

﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a deviator with information...﴾.

Also, there is a special address to those who believe. It is the third such address, after "O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger" [49:1], and after "O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet" [49:2]. Here it is: "O you who believe, if a defiant one (fasiq, one who has gone beyond obedience) comes to you with news, then verify it" [49:6].

We note that the Qur'anic structure did not combine these three matters in one address and did not use conjunctions. Instead, each command was given its own special address, for greater emphasis and concern.

In the counsel of our master Luqman to his son, he said: "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, association is a tremendous wrong" [31:13].

He also said: "O my son, establish the prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and bear patiently what befalls you; indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination. And do not turn your cheek away from people in arrogance, and do not walk on the earth exultantly; indeed, Allah does not love every arrogant boaster. And be moderate in your walking and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of voices is the braying of donkeys" [31:17-19].

So: he singled out the matter of belief ('aqidah) with a special address because of its importance, and he combined the acts of the limbs into one address because they are on one level of importance in religion.

So: we understand from the repetition of "O you who believe" that it gives each address special importance. The meaning of "if a fasiq comes to you with news..." [49:6]: fasiq is a word derived from our saying "fasaqat al-ruṭbah" (the date came out of its skin). That is, it came out of its skin, and a date that comes out of its skin exposes it to insects and harmful blights.

Likewise, the believer is enveloped by faith, which protects him from the blights of the souls. If he commits fisq (moral deviation), meaning he goes out of the bounds of faith and strays from it, he is afflicted by deadly diseases. Therefore they said of the fasiq that he is one who commits a major sin, or one whose state is unknown.

So if news comes to you, that is, information, from such a fasiq, do not accept what he says. Rather, "verify" [49:6], meaning: establish the truth of this report and of the one who passed it on.

Stop until you clarify the reality of what you heard, so that your judgment on matters is factual, and do not let haste and zeal take you so that you fall into what is forbidden: "verify, lest you harm a people in ignorance, and then become regretful for what you have done" [49:6].

Allah the Exalted commands us to verify here because man is a son of changing circumstances, greatly fluctuating. He may be characterized by truthfulness, yet lie this time, or be characterized by lying, yet tell the truth this time. So verification is a necessary precaution, so that judgment and action afterward come objectively, and we do not fall into the circle of injustice and transgression against others.

Clarify the report of the fasiq: perhaps it concerns something in which he disobeyed Allah, since disobedience is easy for him. If you believed him, you might harm a people who have no sin.

"In ignorance" [49:6]: while you are unaware of the reality of the matter. Then the one who was harmed turns out to be the one with the right, and you are the transgressor. You regret your transgression and your departure from what is right; you regret because you made the one you wronged a person with a right over you.

There is a difference between one who commits a sin in ignorance and one who does it deliberately, and acceptance of repentance depends on the soul's stance toward disobedience. I recall that while we were in France, one of our colleagues was nominated to be sent as a delegate to France. He went there solely for the purpose of knowledge, with no other aims in mind, and there he lodged in the manner of strangers in one of the houses, with a family.

One night a daughter of the family with whom he lodged entered upon him. Perhaps he committed a sin with her in that situation, but he fell into it through ignorance and without planning it.

This is unlike another person who, when he goes to these countries, goes with these matters in mind, and perhaps contacts someone who gives him the addresses of the people of sin.

Therefore Allah the Exalted defines the conditions of accepted repentance, saying: "Repentance with Allah is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon; those, Allah will turn to them in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now,' nor for those who die while they are disbelievers; for those We have prepared a painful punishment" [4:17-18].

Regret for the sin is the first stage of repentance. But regarding the command to verify the report of the fasiq: is it an admonition from the outset, or does it have a cause for which the Qur'an was revealed? They said: rather, it has a cause, namely the incident of al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed him to collect the zakat (obligatory almsgiving) funds from Banu al-Mustaliq.

When he went to them, they all came out to meet him and welcome him, having learned that he was the messenger of the Messenger of Allah. But he feared their gathering in this manner, and feared they might harm him, especially since he had an old blood-money (diyah) obligation toward them from the days of ignorance (jahiliyyah).

So he fled back to the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, they refused to give me the zakat." The Messenger of Allah verified the matter and questioned them. They said: "Rather, we went out to him rejoicing, O Messenger of Allah." Had the Messenger of Allah believed this report, he would have considered them apostates, and perhaps something of unpraiseworthy outcome would have happened.

It is also narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed that Mariyah the Copt, mother of Ibrahim, had a paternal cousin who visited her and entered upon her. This angered him, and he said to Ali: "Take this sword and go to him; if you find him, kill him." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, am I to kill him on your command, or does the witness see what the absent one does not?" Note here Ali's caution (may Allah be pleased with him).

When he went and found him with Mariyah, he raised his sword to kill him. But the man hurried to a palm tree and climbed it, so that Ali's sword could not reach him. Then he threw himself down to the ground and opened his legs until the places of his nakedness appeared to Ali, and Ali saw that he was amsah, meaning he had none of what men have, so he refrained from him.

He went to the Messenger of Allah and informed him of the news. He said: "You have spoken the truth, O Ali; the witness sees what the absent one does not see." We understand from this story that the one who informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of it was a fasiq who intended to slander and defame Umm Ibrahim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 49, verse 7:

The discussion here is related to what happened when the Muslims opposed the Prophet's opinion at Hudaybiyyah. Allah, glorified is He, says to them: ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7]. It is as if He is saying: respect his presence among you, for he is the Messenger of Allah and nothing is hidden from him, because he is supported by Allah, and Allah informs him of the reality. His knowledge of matters is not like your knowledge.

The word ﴿among you...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7] indicates containment, as when you say: the water is in the cup, or the money is in the safe. It is well known that the contained is more precious and more valuable than the container. You are a container for the Messenger of Allah and the method of the Messenger of Allah. For this reason they read ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves...﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128] with a fatha on the fa' (أَنفُسِكُم).

So: the presence of the Messenger of Allah among you is a privilege for you, a protection and a safeguard, because he is connected to his Lord. The Quraysh of Makkah and their chieftains knew this, but obstinacy and arrogance overcame them and kept them from faith.

For this reason, one day Abu Sufyan, al-Harith ibn Hisham and Thabit ibn Qays gathered together while Bilal was calling the adhan for the prayer. Thabit said: "May Allah be pleased with my father, for he died before he saw this sight," meaning that Bilal the black Abyssinian was the one calling the adhan for the Messenger of Allah. al-Harith said: "Did the Messenger of Allah not find anyone other than this black crow to call the adhan?" Abu Sufyan said: "By Allah, I would like to say what you say, but I fear that Allah will inform His Messenger of what I say."

So these people knew the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah, but their contentiousness, obstinacy and pride prevented them from accepting the truth.

Also, you know that our master, the Messenger of Allah, gave his two daughters, Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum, in marriage to two sons of Abu Lahab, and this was before the prophethood. When the enmity between Abu Lahab and the Messenger of Allah intensified, Abu Lahab compelled his two sons to divorce them.

One day one of these two sons met the Messenger of Allah on the road, looked at him, then spat, and the Messenger of Allah noticed what he had done. He invoked a curse against him, saying: "May a dog from the dogs of Allah devour you." This supplication reached Abu Lahab, and he feared for his son. When he set out with a trade caravan to Syria, he gathered its men and said to them: "When you halt to rest, that is, when you stop to spend the night, put my son so-and-so among you, for I fear for him the supplication of Muhammad."

So: he knew that Muhammad was upon the truth and that his supplication was answered. Indeed, they placed him among them when they slept, and Allah sent upon him a fierce lion which snatched him from among them.

Thus the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah was known to these people, and their tongues would overcome them and utter this affirmation. Among that is their saying: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7]. Allah reported about them in His saying: ﴿and they denied them, though their souls had been convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance...﴾ [al-Naml: 14].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would surely be in distress...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7]. Among that is what happened from you at Hudaybiyyah: had he obeyed you in not concluding the treaty, ﴿you would be in distress...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7], meaning that hardship, difficulty and sin would have befallen you.

Similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It grieves him that you suffer hardship...﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128]. It grieves him that he sees you in difficulty, because he is compassionate and merciful towards you. If he sees you in disobedience, he asks forgiveness for you, and if he sees you in obedience, he praises Allah. This continues even after he dies.

﴿But Allah has endeared faith to you and made it appealing in your hearts, and has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7]. Here "But" introduces a qualification of what precedes: that is, the Messenger did not obey you in your insistence on entering Makkah and performing the 'umrah. But Allah endeared faith to you and made it appealing in your hearts, so you returned to the opinion of the Messenger of Allah, did not decide on a matter contrary to his command, and were content with it.

This is the result of Allah's guidance to you, His making faith beloved to you and beautiful in your hearts. Without that, you would have departed from His command and perished through your disobedience to Him. At the same time, ﴿He has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7], and this is among the greatest of Allah's favours upon you.

﴿Those...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7], meaning: those who possess these qualities, so they love faith and hate disbelief, defiance and disobedience. ﴿They are the rightly guided﴾ [al-Hujurat: 7]. Rashid is the plural of rashid, one who adheres to the path of truth and guidance and does not deviate from it. From this comes our saying tarshid al-nafaqat (rationalisation of expenditure) and tarshid al-istihlak (rationalisation of consumption), meaning that we place it in its appropriate position.

Al-Fadl means increase, and what is meant here is that God, exalted is He, has dealt with them with an abundance of His blessings and His generosity.

They said to one of the righteous: "Judge between us." He said: "With justice, or with what is better than justice?" They said: "Is there anything better than justice?" He said: "Better than justice is grace (fadl). Justice is that you take your right, and grace is that you relinquish it out of graciousness."

Likewise, God's blessings upon us come by way of grace (fadl), because the obligation (taklif) with which the Truth has charged us returns to us in benefit, and God gains nothing from it at all, for He, glorified is He, is independent of His creation: obedience does not benefit Him, and disobedience does not harm Him. He created us with His attributes of perfection, so the blessings are not a recompense for obedience; rather, they are pure grace from God.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without measure﴾ [al-Zumar: 10], He named it a reward for them so that they would know that their deed is accepted, and that they will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [al-Hujurat: 8], He is All-Knowing, and His knowledge encompasses everything; nothing of your affair is hidden from Him, and what is secret is open before Him: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19].

So, beware lest your deed be mixed with hypocrisy (nifaq), ostentation (riya'), self-admiration ('ujb), or arrogance (kibriya'). We have said that God, exalted is He, desires the hearts, not merely the actions of the limbs. Then He, glorified is He, is ﴿All-Wise﴾ [al-Hujurat: 8], managing the affairs of His dominion according to the requirements of His wisdom, exalted is He; and the wise (hakim) is one who places a thing in its appropriate position.

The word ﴿طَآئِفَتَانِ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9] is the dual of ṭā'ifa, and it is singular in form, although in meaning it denotes a plurality, like the word qawm (people), whose plural is ṭawā'if. This verse establishes a ruling concerning war and the necessity of reconciliation between the two warring groups, so that wars do not continue among the believers with one another.

We note here that the word ﴿طَآئِفَتَانِ..﴾ is dual. The analogical expectation would be that it say "iqtatalā" (they two fought), but the Qur'an made it plural and said ﴿ٱقْتَتَلُواْ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9]. Why? They said: because the ṭā'ifa, as an organization, is embodied in one person, who is the head of this group; but when fighting breaks out, the individuals of the two groups confront one another, so the fighting is by the totality of the individuals.

The evidence for this is that when He spoke of reconciliation, He returned to the dual form and said ﴿فَأَصْلِحُواْ بَيْنَهُمَا..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9], because the session of reconciliation is not necessarily attended by all the individuals of the group; rather, one person represents them and concludes the reconciliation.

﴿فَإِن بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَىٰ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9] means: after the reconciliation has been completed, one of the two groups transgresses against the other. That is, it oversteps and exceeds the limit in aggression and does not respect the reconciliation. ﴿فَقَاتِلُواْ ٱلَّتِي تَبْغِي..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9] means: to repel it. ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَفِيۤءَ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9] means: returns, ﴿إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9], that is, to the truth.

Thus we have now three groups: two groups that fought, and a group that judges between them by reconciliation. That is because the believing community, as a collective, is entrusted with this task, the task of judging between disputants, and it has what qualifies it for justice and for not leaning or following desires in the process of reconciliation. If these conditions are not present in the judge, reconciliation is not achieved, and matters only worsen and grow more complicated.

It suffices that the one who follows his desire and inclination in judging between the two parties falls from the eyes of all; even the group in whose favour he ruled falsely despises him. Therefore they said of the false witness: heads are raised over the opponent by his testimony, and feet trample on his dignity.

As for His saying, ﴿فَإِن فَآءَتْ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9], that is: after the fighting, it returned to what is right, so you too return to reconciliation ﴿فَأَصْلِحُواْ بَيْنَهُمَا بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُوۤاْ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9]. The meaning is: do not leave the group that has returned to the truth without reconciling between them. It is true that it has returned to the truth, but the dispute still persists, so reconciliation is necessary, lest it hatch another war and the roots of the dispute keep smouldering in the breasts and ignite battles anew.

So: we have prevented the battle first, returned the wrongs to their people, and removed the fuse of war.

The word ﴿وَأَقْسِطُوۤاْ..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9] is from aqsaṭa, yuqsiṭu, so he is muqsiṭ, that is: be just between them ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9], the just ones. There is also qasaṭa, yaqsiṭu, so he is qāsiṭ, that is: unjust. From it is His saying: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلْقَاسِطُونَ فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً﴾ [al-Jinn: 15]. The hamza in aqsaṭa is the hamza of removal (hamzat al-izāla), meaning: he removed injustice and oppression.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 49, verse 10:

This matter has a cause. At Hunayn, they disagreed over something, and this dispute grew between them until it became a separate fight among the foolish ones of the people. They used light weapons in it, such as sticks, palm fronds, and palm spathes (shamarikh). Before it could turn into a real war, the matter reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to them: "That is because the believers are brothers by lineage, from Adam (peace be upon him), and brothers in faith. Brotherhood of lineage is prior, and brotherhood of faith follows it." This means that the disbeliever has the right of brotherhood of lineage, even though he has no right in brotherhood of faith.

Therefore, we say of brotherhood of lineage that they are "brothers," and for faith we say: ﴿brothers, facing one another on couches﴾ [al-Hijr: 47]. Therefore, brotherhood is complete in the brotherhood of faith.

It is related that Mu'awiya's chamberlain came in to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, there is a man at the door asking permission to enter, and he claims to be your brother." Mu'awiya laughed and said: "You have served me such-and-such a time, and you do not know my brothers?" He said: "That is what he told me." He said: "Let him in." When he entered, Mu'awiya asked him: "Which of my brothers are you?" He said: "Your brother from Adam." Mu'awiya laughed and said: "A severed kinship tie! By God, I will be the first to restore it," and he fulfilled his need.

The word "brothers" here draws souls closer and removes between people any class distinction or tribal partisanship. Therefore we find the Qur'anic style, even in the matter of retaliation for the slain, says: ﴿But whoever is pardoned something by his brother, then pursuit should be made in good manner...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178].

It is as if He wishes to remind him that he is his brother despite the enmity and rancor between them. God softens hearts out of concern for the safety of the Muslim community, and because of the high standing of brotherhood in human relations, they said in proverbs: "Many a brother of yours was not born of your mother."

Even some hold that when a person stumbles on the road and meets with harm, he says: "Akh!" as if he is calling upon his brother, meaning any brother nearby who can come to his aid.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And fear Allah that you may be shown mercy﴾ [al-Hujurat: 10], i.e., fear Allah in the process of reconciling the two parties.

﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾ [al-Hujurat: 10]: shown mercy from what? You are shown mercy from the continuation of enmity among the believers. This means the necessity of ending disputes before they grow severe and extend, and in their severity there is harm that afflicts everyone: it afflicts the two disputing parties first, then it spreads to you, as each group sees that you side with the other. Therefore: it is in the interest of the whole society to end enmities and preserve the blood of the believers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 49, verse 11:

We note here that the Qur'an directs the prohibition at "the people" (al-qawm) once, and at "the women" once, and assigns each of them its own prohibition. The reason is that the word qawm is used only for men, because they are the ones who stand over the affairs of the family (yaqumuna 'ala shu'un al-usra). As for the woman, her standing (qiyam) is only over her house. The poet says:

"I do not know, and I do not think I know, whether the people of Hisn are men or women."

So, the word qawm is said of women as well. In another verse, God the Exalted says: ﴿Men are guardians (qawwamun) over women...﴾ [al-Nisa': 34]. Some understand from the word qawwamun that it means domination and beating. Never! Rather, men are qawwamun over women, meaning they stand over their care and the management of their affairs.

For this reason we say to the woman "sitt bayt" (lady of the house), as though the man is the servant who looks after her. We also say: "So-and-so is qa'im (in charge) of this matter," meaning he takes on its hard work.

You recall the story of our master Adam, when God settled him and his wife in the Garden, and Adam violated the command of God. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not remove you from the Garden and [thus] you would be distressed."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 117]. This is an address to Adam and Eve.

The rule is that it should say "fatashqaya" in the dual, but He said ﴿fatashqa﴾ (singular), meaning Adam alone, because the duty of toil, hardship, and bearing the responsibility of the family belongs to the man alone. As for the woman, she has her role in the house, a important role that fills every moment of her life. But what can we do, when they want to suffer alongside the men?

The prohibition of mockery in this verse has a cause concerning men and a cause concerning women. Then the man who was told "make room" and did not make room was not forgotten, and the saying of God the Exalted was revealed concerning him: ﴿When you are told, "Make room in the assemblies," then make room; God will make room for you...﴾ [al-Mujadila: 11].

It is narrated that Umm Salama, the Mother of the Believers (radiya Allahu 'anha), was short. Once she was afflicted with pain in her leg, so she bound it with a piece of cloth, and there was a remnant of it hanging down to the ground which she dragged behind her. 'A'isha and Hafsa saw her in this state. One of them said to the other: "She walks with a tail like the tail of a dog." This reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the verse was revealed.

Therefore, the Exalted says on the Day of Resurrection... A lame man entered upon one of them, and he began to look at him with a mocking glance because of his lameness. The lame man understood his intention and said to him: "Do you blame the craft or do you blame the craftsman?" He silenced him until he regretted his bad manners toward him, and he said: "By God, I wished then that I were like him and he were like me."

When the Exalted God forbids us from mockery, He intends equality among all His creation. All creatures are His creation, His workmanship, and His servants, and none among them is the son of God or has any kinship with God. So why then does some of us mock others?

Beware of mocking people, however lowly they may be compared to you. If you see a fault in religion or in character, correct it and improve it as far as you are able.

If the defect is in creation, in something the created has no part in, then show good manners toward the Creator. By God, if you knew what God has placed for the one afflicted (al-mu'auaf) - meaning the one who has a calamity - you would all wish to be afflicted, for God the Exalted has no son. Rather, He has distributed the causes of His favour among His servants, and if He takes something from one of them, He has compensated him with something better.

Mockery and ridicule occur only from a person who excels in something before a person who is deficient in that same thing: such as the rich mocking the poor, the strong mocking the weak, or the sound in constitution mocking the disabled. This behaviour results from heedlessness of the scale of distinction among all creatures, namely piety (taqwa).

We have said: if you look at all existence, you will find in it a just principle: that each one of us, the sum of God's blessings upon him, equals the sum of the blessings upon any other person. For the Creator, glory be to Him, has distributed His favour among His servants. This one takes 100% in intellect and that one takes 100% in health, yet in the end the total is equal.

This is because God the Exalted does not want duplicate copies of humans. Rather He wants us varied in talents, so that the movement of life is set right, it is completed, and humans are bound to one another by the bond of need. For this reason we said that the pasha may need the sewage worker.

His saying the Exalted: ﴿And He raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ [al-An'am: 165] means each of us is elevated in something and is surpassed in something else. You know that Beethoven, the famous musician, was deaf and could not hear, and that Timur Lenk, who shook the world with conquests, was lame.

This means that you should not mock anyone or belittle anyone because you see him less than you in some respect, for we are all equal in the scale of the Truth, glory be to Him. It is as though He wants to give us a lesson that He has no son and no consort.

That is why the jinn had better understanding than us when they said: ﴿And that He, exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has not taken a companion or a son﴾ [al-Jinn: 3]. We are all the dependents of God. Indeed, this equality reaches the point that the Messenger of God commands us to treat our children equally, even in kissing.

Our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), teaches us how to behave if something of mockery or derision occurs between us, and how to confront it and respond to it. It is narrated concerning the occasion of revelation of these verses... look how the Messenger of God dealt with this situation, and how he elevated the standing of Safiyya, the descendant of prophets and the wife of a prophet. Indeed, a response that silences and that no one would think of, and why not, when he (ﷺ) was given the comprehensive words (jawami' al-kalim).

A similar situation also occurred... Some say: how could all this happen in the house of the Messenger of God? We say: from this jealousy we understand, besides that it is a sign of love for the Messenger of God, that 'A'isha, whom the Messenger of God married when she was nine years old, was nevertheless jealous of him despite his age, and this means that he (ﷺ) was not an unwanted man.

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And do not defame one another, and do not insult each other by nicknames...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11]: here is a prohibition of another blameworthy trait unbecoming of the people of faith, namely the trait of lamz, which is to find fault with others. Consider the precision of the Qur'anic expression in His saying: ﴿And do not defame yourselves...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11]. A person does not defame himself, but rather defames others; yet He has placed others in the position of the person himself. Then, when you defame people, you embolden them to defame you, in the words of the poet:

"Do not let your tongue mention the faults of a man, for you are all faults, and people have tongues."

"And if your eye shows you faults, guard it, and say: O eye, people also have eyes."

Also among this is His saying: ﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another...﴾ [al-Nur: 61], because when you greet people, they return the greeting to you, so it is as if you have greeted yourself.

His saying the Exalted: ﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11] is another prohibition against nicknaming (al-tanabuz bi'l-alqab). That is: let none of you call his brother by a title he dislikes. Tanabuz comes from nabaza al-shay', meaning he removed it and abandoned it. Likewise, when you call a person by a nickname he dislikes, you are as though pushing him away from you and widening the gap between you and him.

Names in our language are of three kinds: ism (name), laqab (nickname), and kunya (patronymic). The ism is what is applied to the named so that it becomes a proper name, such as Muhammad. The laqab is what indicates praise or blame, such as al-Siddiq, or as when we call one of the weak, for example, "Sulayman Batta." As for the kunya, it begins with "Abu" or "Umm," such as Abu Bakr and Umm al-Mu'minin.

Thus: it is not permissible to call a person by a word he dislikes and does not wish to be called by, such as what we mentioned of 'A'isha's words to Safiyya: "O Jewess." Nicknaming sows resentment and rancour, and stirs up the instincts and anger against you. Why not call him by the names most beloved to him, so as to incline him toward you?

The jurists even said: if a man commits a sin and then repents of it, beware of reminding him of it or reproaching him with it, for that counts as slander (qadhf) against him, besides which you would be helping Satan against him. Like someone who repented from wine and we call him "ya khamurji" (O drunkard), or who repented from gambling and we call him "ya qamarati" (O gambler), and so on.

Therefore He said after it: ﴿Wretched is the name of wickedness after faith...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11]. That is: how evil is what you say to your brother when you remind him of a past he wants to forget; and it is ugly for you to reproach him after he has repented, just as it is ugly for you to commit wickedness after faith.

﴿And whoever does not repent...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11], meaning from nicknaming, ﴿those are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11]. Yes, they are wrongdoers to themselves by not following the method in this prohibition, and wrongdoers to others when they call them by these disliked titles. So the one who has repented has the right that you do not remind him of his fault, and that you do not reproach him with it.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 49, verse 12:

Allah, glory be to Him, commands us to avoid much of suspicion (ẓann), and ẓann is a thought that occurs to the mind. It is of two kinds: good suspicion (ẓann ḥasan) and bad suspicion (ẓann sayyi'). Good suspicion has nothing wrong in it and no sin upon it; rather, it is among the things the Sharia enjoins, as we shall see. The thing forbidden here is bad suspicion, which leads to corruption in relations and entails punishment.

Therefore our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), taught us to avoid bad suspicion. Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) teaches us to close the door of bad suspicion, to cut off its causes, and to protect ourselves from placing ourselves in that position.

In the story of the slander (al-ifk) in Surah al-Nur, Allah teaches us and urges us to think well of the believers and to keep away from bad suspicion about them. Concerning their talk about the matter of Sayyida 'Aisha, He says: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind and say, "This is an obvious falsehood"?﴾ [al-Nur: 12].

Good suspicion means that you take precaution in a matter and do not let it leave a bad impression on your soul. For example, if a man comes to you and says: "On this road there is a group lying in wait for you who intend you harm," you should take the more cautious course for yourself, believe him, and beware of what he warned you about, because the likelihood is that he wants your safety, not your harm.

As for when suspicion entails a legal ruling, then it becomes obligatory for you to verify its truth.

Consider the precision and caution of the Qur'anic expression in His words: ﴿much of suspicion..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12], meaning: most suspicion is bad suspicion, which must be avoided, and a little of it is good suspicion, to which there is no objection. Therefore He said after it: ﴿indeed, some suspicion is sin..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12], not all of it. So beware of falling into sin when you think ill of the believers without evidence.

His words: ﴿and do not spy..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12] mean: do not pursue people's faults and do not search for their private matters. And in a hadith: ...

We mention here a delicate point about the Beautiful Names of Allah. You will notice that many of His names have opposites, as in al-Muhyi (the Giver of Life) and al-Mumit (the Causer of Death), al-Mu'izz (the Exalter) and al-Mudhill (the Abaser), al-Qabid (the Withholder) and al-Basit (the Extender).

But does al-Sattar (the Concealer) have an opposite, meaning "the Exposer"? Exalted is Allah above this attribute, for His concealment is drawn over His servants whatever they do; He does not expose them. Al-Sattar is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) from the root s-t-r, "to conceal."

Therefore a hadith has come, the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah conceals and loves concealment." [The rest of the hadith as it stands in the text is not fully given here.] I dislike the disobedient person, but I dislike even more the one who pursues him. Why? Because tracking down faults and slips spreads indecency in society.

Thus Allah protects the community of faith from this, and it is enough that one who conceals his sin still has the modesty of faith.

The Prophet (ﷺ) says: ...

This is like someone who cannot fast, for example, and has a valid excuse and is permitted to break the fast, yet still may not openly break it before people, so that he does not become a bad example for young people who do not understand these excuses.

When they see him breaking the fast, a mental precedent takes root in them that it is permissible for them to break the fast in Ramadan. Therefore he must conceal his breaking of the fast so that this example does not take place.

Because of the gravity of spying, the jurists said: if a man lives in a hut of reeds and palm stalks, and another comes and looks at him through the gaps, then the owner of the hut takes a stick and blinds his eye, there is no retaliation or compensation for his eye, because the first man had intruded upon his home and looked at him without his permission.

A similar case is found in the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when it reached him that a man was looking at him through a hole in the door.

It is related that our master 'Umar used to inspect the conditions of his subjects and patrol at night. It reached him that a man was drinking wine with his companions in his house, so he climbed over the wall of his house and found him sitting with a man of his companions, and there was no wine in the gathering nor anything of that sort.

When the man saw him he said: "You have thought of me such and such, but you have overlooked matters of religion more important than that. First: you entered the house over the wall, and Allah says: ﴿And enter houses through their doors..﴾ [al-Baqara: 189]. Second: you entered my house without seeking permission." So 'Umar departed and said nothing.

There is a difference between tajassus (with jim) and tahassus (with ha'). Tahassus is seeking and searching for others, but without targeting their private faults. Of this is His saying: ﴿O my sons, go and seek out news of Yusuf and his brother..﴾ [Yusuf: 87], meaning: search for him until you reach him, as intelligence officers do, for example.

His words: ﴿and do not backbite one another..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12] are a general prohibition of backbiting (ghiba), because the Qur'an did not specify who backbites or about whom.

Then the Qur'an gives us a tangible image of backbiting, saying: ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12]. Consider how many repellent elements there are in this image that show the atrocity of this act. The one who backbites his brother in his absence is like one who eats his flesh while he is dead, that is, absent from life and unable to defend himself.

So He likened it to a hideous image from which a sound soul recoils.

It is said that the cause of revelation of this verse is that it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, when the Messenger of Allah sent him to collect zakat from the Banu al-Mustaliq, and he had owed them blood-money in the pre-Islamic period. When they saw him they came out to meet him, so he feared retaliation from them, returned to the Messenger of Allah, and said that they had refused to pay zakat.

It is also related that Usama ibn Zayd was in charge of the provisions in the house of the Messenger of Allah. Two men wanted to go and eat in the house of the Messenger of Allah, so they sent Salman al-Farisi to ask Usama for food. When he asked him, Usama said: "We have no food." Salman returned to them and said: "Usama says we have no food." They said: "Rather, he has it but is stingy with it." Then they said to Salman: "You have an ill-omened face; if you had gone to the well of Sumayh" (meaning: Fawwar), "its water would have disappeared."

Thus they backbit both Usama and Salman. When the Messenger of Allah saw them he said: "I smell the odour of putrid flesh from your mouths." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, we have not eaten any flesh." He said: "You have backbitten Usama and Salman. Go and appease them, for if you do not appease the one you have backbitten, you will be worse in Allah's sight than the adulterer."

Therefore, when a man backbit Ibn Sirin, he came to him and said: "O Imam, release me from my backbiting of you." He said: "Why?" He said: "Because I backbit you." He said: "I do not release what Allah has forbidden."

And al-Hasan al-Basri learned that a man had backbitten him, so he sent to him his servant with a tray of fresh dates, and said: "Tell him: this is a gift to you from my master, because he knew that you had given him your good deeds yesterday."

This shows that you pay the right of the one you have backbitten from your good deeds; if you have no good deeds, some of his evil deeds are taken and cast upon you, and the noble hadith has indicated this.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12] mean: fear Allah in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you, and avoid the causes of His punishment. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12], that is, He is abundant in accepting the repentance of whoever repents, abundant in mercy toward whoever turns back.

This conclusion gives the sinner hope in Allah's mercy, and does not despair the backbiters of His mercy, glory be to Him. Whoever slips in his tongue into backbiting should hasten to repentance, and when he knows that his Lord is Accepting of repentance and Merciful, he returns soon and does not savour this deed nor persist in it.

We have already explained that among the greatest of Allah's blessings upon us is that He prescribed repentance for us and opened for us the door of acceptance; otherwise the sinners would persist and life would be corrupted.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says:

﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female...﴾.

Note that the earlier calls to address were "O you who have believed," because they are directives and legislation specific to those who believe, since God only holds accountable those who believe in Him.

The address here, however, is a general call to all people, drawing our attention to the sign of creation and the greatness of the Creator, may He be glorified. This verse includes everyone. The Creator, glorified is He, created the believer and the disbeliever, the male and the female, and they are the origin of this creation, for the male alone does not reproduce, and neither does the female alone.

As for His saying in Surat al-Sajdah: ﴿Who perfected everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay. Then He made his descendants from an extract of a liquid, despised.﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7-8], this refers to the first creation, Adam, peace be upon him, whom God created and formed with His own hands. Everything in the universe is subject to His decree: "Be," and it is.

Therefore God said to Iblis: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands?..﴾ [Sad: 75]. That is: how is it that you do not prostrate to something I created with My own hands? So you do not prostrate to Adam; rather, you prostrate in obedience to the One who commanded you to prostrate.

After He created Adam from clay, He made his offspring from after him ﴿from an extract of a liquid, despised﴾ [al-Sajdah: 8], and this necessitates the pairing of male and female.

In Surat al-Nisa, He, glorified is He, said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul..﴾ [al-Nisa: 1], that is Adam, peace be upon him, ﴿and created from it its mate..﴾ [al-Nisa: 1], that is Eve. Therefore, when He says: ﴿from male and female..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13], it does not refer to the beginning of creation, but to the offspring that came after the first creation.

Therefore, at the end of the verse in al-Nisa He said: ﴿and dispersed from both of them many men and women..﴾ [al-Nisa: 1]. These men and women spread throughout the earth and became ﴿nations and tribes..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13]. The Arabs are a nation, the Romans are a nation, the Persians are a nation. Then the nations divided into tribes, the tribes into clans, the clans into lineages, and so on.

Within a single family, names differ, because we do not leave individuals without names so that they may be recognized. This is Muhammad, this is Ahmad, and this is Fatimah... The wisdom behind this is ﴿that you may know one another..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13], at the level of individuals and at the level of peoples.

Getting to know one another is a necessity among humankind, because their interests lie in their knowing one another. The circumstances of life will compel them to this acquaintance, since some will need others. As we have said, God, glorified is He, distributed the causes of His bounty among His creation, so what is available to you may not be available to others.

For example, we have seen Europe, which has reached such a level of civilization and progress that it needs the inhabitants of the desert, the herders of sheep and camels, where there is oil, and the wealth of the mountains: minerals and precious stones.

This difference in virtues leads to creation cooperating and supporting one another, so that some complete the deficiency of others. In sum: a difference that leads to complementarity, not to hostility.

We have witnessed this complementarity in the creation of man and woman. Man and woman are not opposites; rather, they are two complementary elements, because each has a function that the other does not perform.

God, glorified is He, clarified this matter for us in His saying: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾ [al-Layl: 1-2]. Would any sensible person say that night is the opposite of day?

Like night and day are male and female. Therefore, He swore after them by their creation, saying: ﴿And by He who created the male and female﴾ [al-Layl: 3]. Man is for bearing life's hardships, for toil and work, while woman is tenderness and emotion, and each is made easy for what they were created for.

So we are amazed at those who call for equality between men and women, how can that be, when each has their own function for which they were created? Some wrong women and say: "deficient in intellect and religion," because intellect's function is ordering and choosing between alternatives, and this is not the function of women but of men, who steer the household through the journey of life.

As for women, their function is emotional: they show tenderness to the young and old, open their hearts to contain, and comfort the weary and the sick in their families. Yet we see that when a woman is widowed, she performs both roles and takes the place of the husband, and perhaps she is even more successful in raising and protecting the children.

God, glorified and exalted is He, created Adam from clay, shaped him, and breathed into him of His spirit. But He did not create Eve in the same way; rather, He took a part from Adam's rib and created Eve from it. Why then did He not create her like Adam? They said: He created her from the man so that he would have guardianship (qawamah) over her.

Likewise, in the matter of pregnancy, she takes the seed from him, then she completes the process of reproduction. God said: ﴿and created from it its mate..﴾ [al-Nisa: 1].

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Just as Adam was honored in that God created him and formed him with His own hand, so Eve was honored in that she was created from something God created with His own hand."

The world is now preoccupied with the process of cloning (istinsakh), which means taking from the original an identical copy of it, just as we say "copying a book." That is, bringing from it another image like it. We see this process in inanimate things, for example. We see pebbles, large, small and medium. Have we ever seen a pebble grow beyond its size, ever? Why?

They say: because it has hidden reservoirs beneath the earth in which this process of multiplication or cloning takes place. When it comes out into the air, it stays as it is.

We find the same in plants. Have you seen, for example, seeds of sugarcane or of the Barshumi fig? Never, it has no seeds. Rather, we take a cutting from a sugarcane stalk and plant it, and a sugarcane stalk grows. We take a shoot of a fig and plant it, and it yields a fig tree. Is this not cloning?

Likewise, it is possible to find it in animals. Indeed, they have spoken about cloning that has actually been carried out in animals, as happened with the sheep Dolly. In any case, it is an attempt.

As for humans, it is a process no one can achieve, because the human being differs from the rest of the kinds of the universe. He is God's vicegerent on earth, the honored creature, and the other kinds are at his service. So if we imagine cloning in inanimate things, plants, and animals, we cannot imagine it at all in humans, because reproduction in humans has conditions and controls, not merely the extraction of duplicate copies of them.

Therefore, human reproduction takes place only through the union of the male and female spouses, and within a family that embraces the child, loves him, raises him, and cares for him. It is not fitting for a human being to come out of a hatchery like a chicks' hatchery, for example.

Therefore, we see that human childhood is the longest childhood among all creatures. Among our children are those whose childhood lasts until the age of 14. As for birds and animals, they care for their young until they can move and eat, then they leave them as if they do not know them, and an animal may be slaughtered in front of its mother while she is unaware of it.

So how then can we imagine cloning in human beings, who are the honored vicegerent? All religions reject fornication and refuse that a child come by an illegitimate way; they refuse that a newborn be thrown into the street, or even raised in orphanages. How much more so if he were cloned?

From here we say: the process of cloning will never take place in human beings, and no one is capable of it except God, the Creator of man, who wills good for him. He wills that he come into the embrace of a father who cares for him and a mother who tenderly looks after him, from whom he takes virtues and learns values.

Moreover, their success in cloning an animal does not at all imply a challenge to divine power; rather, it is a new proof of faith in that power. The one who cloned the sheep did not bring her from nothing; he brought her from another sheep, which is itself a creature of God, and the mind that thought is itself a creation of God.

Then God, glorified is He, lays down the principle by which these nations and tribes are distinguished, saying: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13]. That is: the individuals of the nations are distinguished by piety.

Therefore, it is related in the Hadith Qudsi: and His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13], Knowing of His creation, giving each of them what suits his function and role in the movement of life, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].

God knows His creation best, and knows their abilities and their measure. He has made easy for each of them the work that suits him. Therefore, we see them in classes: among them is the university professor, and among them the blacksmith, the plumber, the carpenter, and the shoe-shiner, among them the craftsman and the farmer. Otherwise, how would the movement of life be sound if all people were university graduates?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 49, verse 14:

Al-A'rab (the Bedouins): a collective noun with no singular form. Al-A'rab are the inhabitants of the desert who did not go to settled towns; for this reason we find them in their natural state, in which harshness prevails over them. Almighty Allah informs us that they said, ﴿We have believed.﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14], and Allah, glory be to Him, knows best that they had not reached the level of faith, because faith is not a word that is spoken but a firmly established conviction that fills the heart.

As for Islam, it is the outward form and the action of the limbs, such as fasting, prayer and other acts of worship. Therefore He corrected their statement and said: ﴿Say: You have not believed; but say, "We have submitted",﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14].

Meaning: you only carry out the commands of Islam through the actions of your limbs, while there is no faith in your hearts. When He says to them, ﴿You have not believed﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14], this is evidence that it struck something in their souls, and nothing among His servants is hidden from Him, and they know this reality.

So: He informed them of a reality within their souls, saying to them: Be truthful with yourselves and say, "We have submitted", while Allah knows the unseen of your hearts. In this situation they resemble the hypocrites, who were keen to pray in the first row and to listen attentively to the recitation of the Qur'an; these are all outward appearances, while Allah knows their inner secrets and knows that they are contrary to what they display.

His saying: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]. Lamma (لما) is a negating particle like (lam), it negates the occurrence of the action in the past relative to the speaker, but it also conveys another meaning, namely the possibility that the action will occur afterwards, as when you enter a garden and say: "The garden has not yet borne fruit", meaning that it will bear fruit later.

For this reason the scholars said regarding this verse: it did not close the door of faith in their faces, and it gave good news that they would believe later. Moreover, the Qur'an's disclosure of what was concealed in their hearts, and the Messenger's informing them of it, is what made them reflect on the matter, become convinced, and enter the realm of faith.

His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds at all﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]. Almighty Allah reassures them regarding the fruit of their righteous deeds: it is preserved and will not be lost, nor will it even be diminished.

The meaning of ﴿He will not deprive you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14] is: He will not reduce anything of your deeds. The verb is: alta, yalit.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]. In another place He says: ﴿And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving﴾ [Saba: 2]. Sometimes He puts mercy first and sometimes forgiveness, according to the situation.

For example, when a culprit stands before the ruler admitting his sin, but the ruler notices that he is in a wretched state, with worn clothing and a pale complexion, he takes pity on him, then orders food and clothing for him. After that he pardons him.

Here he placed mercy before forgiveness, or the reverse: he pardons him first, then before he leaves the assembly he tells his men: give him such-and-such.

This root (alt) occurs elsewhere in His saying: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants and We will not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾ [al-Tur: 21]. The discussion here concerns a group of believers, and their descendants follow them; likewise in faith they share it. So what is the necessity of joining here?

They said: We join them to them in reward, because each of them has deeds, but the deeds of the fathers are greater and their rank is higher; as an honour to them, We join the children to them and make them all in one rank, so the lower is raised to the higher.

His saying: ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]: in what? You obey Him in faith, because they were in fact Muslims, so He wished to urge them toward faith and keep them away from lying and pretension.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 49, verse 15:

Allah, glory be to Him, wishes to clarify for them the meaning of faith (iman), and that it is not merely a word that is spoken, but a firmly rooted conviction into which neither doubt nor suspicion can enter. ﴿Those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then they do not doubt...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 15]. They believe in Allah and in His oneness, and that He, glory be to Him, alone is the Creator, the Provider, the One who manages the affairs of this universe. They believe in the names and attributes of Allah. Likewise, they believe in the Messenger of Allah, and that he is trustworthy and truthful in conveying from Allah. Then they do not doubt or waver concerning any of this.

Among the attributes of the believers also is ﴿and strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 15]. And is there anything that more clearly proves the truthfulness of faith and sincerity in it than that you give your very self for the sake of this faith?

For this reason He said ﴿Only the believers are...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 15], meaning: the believers in the true sense of faith, these are their attributes. Then at the end of the verse He describes them as truthful in their faith.

﴿Those are the truthful ones﴾ [al-Hujurat: 15]. Yes, they are truthful in their faith, because they sacrificed what is most precious and dear that a person possesses: first wealth, then the self. The martyr does not sacrifice his self or offer his wealth except while certain that he will find with Allah something better than what he left in this world.

For this reason his Lord rewards him with everlasting life, so that death does not reach him afterwards: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169].

That is, they are treated as the people of Paradise are treated: they eat, drink, and enjoy themselves. Note that Allah, glory be to Him, described this life by His saying ﴿alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169], not "with you."

This means that if you were to open the grave of a martyr, you would not find him alive, because he is not alive with you; rather, he is alive with Allah.

And in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Those are the truthful ones﴾ [al-Hujurat: 15] there is an allusion to those who lied against Allah and claimed faith, as if He were saying to them: Those people believed and were truthful in their faith, but as for you, you have lied and exceeded the truth.

The meaning: pay heed to this truth. I am your Creator, and I know you better than you know yourselves, and nothing among you is hidden from Me. So beware of saying "We have believed" while thinking that you can conceal the truth and cover up your lie. I know the believer from the non-believer; I know the truthful and I know the hypocrite.

﴿Say: Will you inform Allah about your religion?...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 16]. That is: will you tell Him of what you are upon of faith, [when] ﴿Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth...﴾ [al-Hujurat: 16]. That is: nothing in them is hidden from Him. Rather, ﴿Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Hujurat: 16]. The meaning: His knowledge, exalted is He, does not stop at the heavens and the earth; it extends beyond that.

﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Hujurat: 16]. This is because the heavens and the earth are only a part of Allah's vast creation. For this reason He described them, that is the heavens and the earth and what is between them, saying: like a ring thrown down in a desert. What we know of the heavens and the earth is hardly worth mentioning in the creation of Allah.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have accepted Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favour to me. Rather, Allah confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you are truthful...﴾.

It is related that this verse was revealed concerning a group of Bedouins, and it is said: from the tribe of Banu Asad. They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the mosque, and said: "We have come to you bearing witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah. You did not send any expedition to us, and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so fought you."

So Allah revealed: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favour to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favour upon you, that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful."﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17].

So then: who is bestowing a favour upon whom? You should not regard your Islam as a favour to the Messenger of Allah, because your Islam returns its benefit to yourselves. Islam is what has granted you security from fighting, war and captivity, and you have obtained what distinguishes the Muslim in terms of rights to zakat and protection. Allah, exalted is He, is not benefited by obedience, nor harmed by disobedience.

So then: do not regard your Islam as a favour ﴿Rather, Allah has conferred a favour upon you..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17], because He has guided you to the path of rectitude and right guidance ﴿that He has guided you to faith..﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17]. So then: if there is any favour, the favour is Allah's upon you, because obedience to Allah and walking in His way is what protects for you the movement of life and organises it so that your interests do not conflict.

﴿if you are truthful﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17], i.e., in your claim to faith. The word "in" (in) indicates doubt, as if they were conferring a favour in respect of something about which they are lying. And even if they were truthful, it would not have been permissible for them to confer a favour on account of it.

Earlier we explained that the heavens and the earth are a container, and within this container are wonders and marvels of God's creation that are greater than the container itself, because the rule is that the contained is higher and greater than that which contains it.

Therefore the Almighty says: ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [Al-Imran: 189], and in another place: ﴿And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth...﴾ [An-Najm: 31]. So the heavens and the earth, despite the wonders of creation, innovation and cosmic engineering they contain, hold something even more wondrous.

Here the Almighty tells us about the unseen (ghayb) that is in the heavens and the earth. The unseen is everything that is hidden from your perception. A thing may be hidden from your perception today and become apparent to you tomorrow. For example, electricity before its discovery was an unseen matter about which we knew nothing, and now it has become a visible reality that we all sense and deal with.

If you were to consider the carriers that bear sound and image through the air, you would find a truly marvellous matter. For if you were to bring, for example, a hundred radios and a hundred televisions, place them in one place, and direct each one toward a different direction, you would find different transmissions of sound and image.

How, then, do these waves interpenetrate in one air, and reach us with this precision and clarity, while they come from the farthest parts of the world?

All of these are secrets from the unseen of the heavens and the earth, which call us to belief in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth...﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

And despite the greatness of creation in the heavens and the earth, the unseen of the heavens and the earth is greater than all of it, and this unseen will remain an inexhaustible supply and an endless bounty, which reveals to us from time to time something new from God's unseen, so that the Qur'an remains miraculous until the Hour arrives.

From the wisdom of the Almighty and Exalted is that He distributed the bounties of the Qur'an across all the ages of time, so that no age receives the Qur'an empty of bounty.

Moreover, this bounty comes in proportion to minds, and in proportion to research and reflection upon God's dominion. Thus we understand the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Qur'an: For example, you may read the greatest poems, and you are bound to grow weary of them after one time or even after several times. But you read the Qur'an and do not tire of it; rather, your love for it increases the more you contemplate its recitation, because it is the Word of God, and it has a secret with every one who recites it, and a bounty for every one who reflects upon it. The bounties of the Qur'an are many; each reciter takes from it according to his measure.

The conclusion of the surah with this verse, ﴿Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 18], indicates that the dominion of God is vast, and His wonders do not end, and have no limit or count. However advanced mankind becomes, the new will remain with the Qur'an, and in the signs of God is what dazzles the minds.

In the past we used to speak of the age of coal, then the age of steam, then the age of electricity, and now they speak of the age of nuclear energy and atomic energy. Where were these energies?

They were unseen in the knowledge of God, and He revealed them to His servants when minds advanced and ideas rose. All of these are discoveries that no one brought from himself; all of them are from God, and an overflow of His bounty kept hidden until its time.
